text:
maya: hey team — quick heads up, our quantized candidate q4_0 shows a better calibration curve in CI (Brier down ~0.03) but manual spot checks per-language look worse. did something change in the eval runner aggregations?
sam: ugh that's worrying. which metric exactly — sample-weighted Brier or macro-avg?
maya: CI reports "brier_overall" which I think is the sample-weighted Brier computed per-bucket then averaged. but when I split by lang, most languages have worse brier.
devon: could be a binning/aggregation bug. I vaguely remember a recent change to how we compute bin counts (np.histogram vs np.digitize) for speed.
liam: can you paste the runner snippet that computes calibration?
maya: pasted below — this is the current code in eval/metrics/calibration.py in CI (abbrev). not sure about edge behavior on bin boundaries.

```
# simplified
bins = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, 11)
bin_idx = np.digitize(pred_probs, bins)  # 1..len(bins)
counts, _ = np.histogram(pred_probs, bins=bins, density=True)
brier_per_bin = ((pred_probs - labels)**2).groupby(bin_idx).mean()
overall = (brier_per_bin * counts).sum() / counts.sum()
```

sam: ohhh density=True in np.histogram returns density (pdf), not raw counts. multiplying mean by density then summing is wrong. that would favor buckets differently across languages if sample sizes differ.
devon: exactly — density normalizes area under histogram to 1, so you end up weighting by bin width and not sample count. on top of that, digitize with the default right=False puts a value equal to a bin edge into the next bin sometimes. both can flip small-language stats.
liam: nice catch. also if pred_probs contains exactly 1.0 or 0.0 then digitize returns len(bins) which may index out of range in the groupby.
maya: wow. that explains CI showing improvement — global density-normalized brier can move independently from per-language sample-weighted brier.
sam: propose quick patch: replace density=True with density=False and use counts = np.bincount(bin_idx, minlength=len(bins)+1)[1:-1] (to match digitize indexing). also clamp probs to [1e-12, 1-1e-12] and use right=True for digitize to keep edges deterministic.

```
# proposed
bins = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, 11)
bin_idx = np.digitize(np.clip(pred_probs, 1e-12, 1-1e-12), bins, right=True)
counts = np.bincount(bin_idx, minlength=len(bins)+1)[1:-1]
brier_per_bin = ((pred_probs - labels)**2).groupby(bin_idx).mean()
overall = (brier_per_bin * counts).sum() / counts.sum()
```

devon: LGTM. add a test with a few deterministic probs to assert counts and bin assignment. also add a regression test that computes both sample-weighted and macro-avg and ensure CI reports both so we surface language regressions.
liam: I'll open a small PR and add the unit tests + a dashboard change to show per-lang brier and global-weighted brier separately.
maya: thanks. can we also re-run the failing quantization run with the fixed runner to confirm the earlier result?
eval-bot: re-run triggered for job: eval-quant-q4_0-2334567001 (logs will appear in ~10m).
liam: opened PR #1429 with patches + tests. pinging @sam @devon for quick review.
sam: reviewing now. covers edge cases? feel free to add a note in CHANGELOG about diagnosis.
maya: once merged, can someone reindex the dashboard calc? our dashboard uses precomputed aggregates in s3 for last 30 days.
devon: I'll kick off the reindex job after merge. also we'll add a smoke check in CI that compares runner output for a small seed against a golden file to catch density/normalization regressions.
liam: PR merged and deploy job started.
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded to staging (deploy-2026-07-12T15:04Z).
maya: re-run results: q4_0 now shows brier overall slightly worse (consistent with per-lang), so the quant hurt calibration. thanks for the catch — saved us a bad rollout. :relieved: 
sam: great. next: think about adding temperature-aware sampling notes to the eval docs — gets subtle with pass@k.
maya: noted. I'll create a follow-up thread for pass@k sampling and temp effects. thanks everyone!
